messages:
maria: Heads-up — kicked off a bakeoff comparing FP8 / INT8-GPTQ / AWQ (act-quant) for redwood-open-13b on the standard eval corpus. Seeing weird instability on serving when act-quant is enabled with group_size=128.

jun: What kind of instability? accuracy drop or hangs?

maria: Both. Intermittent output quality regressions on long-context QA (QA-acc down ~1.8% vs FP8 baseline on the canary set) and occasional char-level hangs where the stream stalls for ~200-400ms mid-response.

sam: Do you have the eval numbers?

maria: Pasted short table from the run: 
```
Baseline FP8 (quantized): QA acc 86.1%, tail P50 latency 62ms
GPTQ (int8): QA acc 85.3%, tail P50 68ms
AWQ act-quant gsz=128: QA acc 84.3%, tail P50 78ms (sporadic stalls)
AWQ act-quant gsz=32: QA acc 85.7%, tail P50 66ms
```

rachel: Interesting — group_size drop to 32 recovered most of the quality and latency?

maria: Yes, but we still saw a couple of stalls in the gsz=32 canary. Stalls correlate with certain token entropy patterns (high-sampling entropy).

aria: Any logs from the runtime around a stall?

maria: Snippet from the canary host logs during a stall: 
```
[2026-03-19T22:11:08Z] serve: WARN prefix_cache_miss uid=abc123 seq=1024
[2026-03-19T22:11:08Z] runtime: INFO group_exec gsz=128 actq=on batch=1
[2026-03-19T22:11:09Z] runtime: ERROR kv_cache_resize failed: LAZY_ALLOC_BACKOFF
[2026-03-19T22:11:09Z] stream: WARN token_emit_delay ms=380
```

jun: kv_cache_resize failed looks like memory pressure with gsz=128. Could be prealloc assumptions in the AWQ path.

maria: Agreed. I repro'd locally by running sustained concurrency=12 with gsz=128 and seed fixed; memory occasionally spikes.

sam: Did you try enabling kv prealloc or lowering max_batch?

maria: Yes — enabling `--kv-prealloc=true` removed the LAZY_ALLOC_BACKOFF errors but stalls still happened ~rarely. Lowering `--max-batch-tokens` from 2048->1024 helped reduce frequency.

rachel: For quality regression: is the act-quant implementation using asymmetric activation ranges? Any per-channel folding differences vs GPTQ?

maria: AWQ uses blockwise act quant with dynamic scaling. I compared quant stats: AWQ shows 12% higher activation clipping on certain layers vs GPTQ. That correlates with the QA drop.

aria: Could you run a focused ablation: AWQ act-quant but disable activation clipping (or increase clip threshold) + gsz=32?

maria: On it. Running now. Command I'm using: `./run_bakeoff --model redwood-open-13b --strategy awq --act-quant --group-size 32 --kv-prealloc --max-batch-tokens 1024 --seed 42 --keep-clip-scale 1.5`

jun: Also test deterministic prefix-cache warmup and set `--stream-timeout-ms=1200` to avoid stream stalls bubbling to the client.

maria: Result from ablation (quick summary):
```
AWQ actq gsz=32 clip*1.5 kv_prealloc: QA acc 85.9%, tail P50 68ms, stalls=1/2000 requests
AWQ actq gsz=32 clip*2.0 kv_prealloc: QA acc 86.0%, tail P50 69ms, stalls=0/2000
```

sam: That looks promising — increasing clip threshold recovers quality. Any impact on hallucination or logprob calibration?

maria: Small increase in low-confidence tails but no obvious hallucination spike in the eval set. Logprob calibration shift is +0.02 average.

rachel: For deployment profile: I'd run a canary with multi-az routing and set a fallback to FP8 variant on error rate > 0.5% or latency > 2x baseline. Also log sampling-entropy per-request for postmortem.

maria: Proposed rollout plan: 1) internal perf bakeoff with gsz=32 & clip=2.0; 2) 1% canary on Dedicated pool with kv_prealloc & stream-timeout; 3) monitor QA-acc, tail-latency, stalls, error-rate; auto-fallback to FP8 if any metric crosses threshold.

aria: One more curious thing — when we combine AWQ with our prefix cache enabled aggressively, we see fewer stalls but a slight quality regression vs AWQ+no-prefix-cache. Maybe cache re-use is interacting with the act quant numeric dynamics.

jun: That makes sense: prefix cache replays earlier activations which might sit near clipping thresholds and amplify quantization bias. Worth logging `activation_scale` per prefix length in the canary.

maria: I'll add those telemetry fields and run a 24h canary.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: model=redwood-open-13b-awq-g32-clip2.0 pool=dedicated-canary region=us-west-2 pct=1 start_ts=3771234575

sam: Great. If the canary passes, let's draft a short-rolling upgrade that includes flags: `--kv-prealloc=true`, `--group-size=32`, `--act-quant-clip=2.0`, `--stream-timeout-ms=1200` and a 5% safety net fallback to FP8 variant.

maria: Thanks all — will post back with the 24h telemetry and samples for any weird failures.

rachel: Thx, useful thread. If anyone sees unexplained stalls, ping me & I'll pull host flamegraphs. :mag:
